programme: MAML1 is the obligate coactivator that converts Notch1 signaling into transcription (HES1, HEY1, NOTCH1 among its targets); SMAD1 is the BMP-branch SMAD that also converges on HEY1 and drives ECM/angiogenic effectors (MMP1, MMP2, VEGFA, BMP2/7, ACVR1); HOXA11 sits downstream/parallel, sharing the MMP2 remodeling target with SMAD1 and independently sustaining a HOX-driven progenitor programme. Together they form a Notch–BMP/SMAD–HOX axis that sets the balance between progenitor self-renewal/proliferation and differentiation or vascular remodeling, with HEY1 and MMP2 as the concrete convergence points in the target data.
role_in_a: In AML, Notch1 signaling through its MAML1 coactivator sustains proliferation and delays differentiation of myeloid progenitors (PMID 30086426); loss of the counterbalancing SMAD1 (BMP arm) cooperates with KMT2A-rearrangements to drive leukemogenesis (PMID 39834944); HOXA11 sustains the leukemic transcriptional state and modulates chemosensitivity to cytarabine (PMID 34080665).
role_in_b: In stroke, SMAD1 acting through BMP6/SMAD1/5/9 promotes cerebral angiogenesis and vascular repair after ischemia (PMID 40274709); the HOXA11 locus (via its antisense transcript HOXA11-AS) modulates ischemic neuronal death (PMID 37059588). No retrieved evidence places MAML1/Notch activity in stroke.
shared_axis: Both the leukemic bone-marrow niche and the post-ischemic brain depend on a progenitor/vascular fate decision between self-renewal (or neuronal survival) and differentiation/angiogenic commitment; the same Notch–BMP-SMAD-HOX wiring that gates hematopoietic progenitor fate in AML is redeployed to gate neurovascular repair after stroke, rather than the two diseases sharing a documented causal link.
reasoning: SMAD1 is independently and mechanistically documented in both diseases (AML via KMT2A-fusion cooperation, stroke via BMP-driven angiogenesis), and the module (Notch/MAML1-BMP/SMAD1 convergence on HEY1, plus HOX/SMAD1 convergence on MMP2) is nameable from the target lists themselves. But MAML1's AML evidence is indirect (a NOTCH1, not MAML1, paper) with no stroke evidence at all, HOXA11's stroke evidence concerns a distinct antisense transcript with a different endpoint (neuronal death, not angiogenesis), and no source discusses AML and stroke together through this axis — the cross-disease link rests on pathway logic, not retrieved fact.
support: PMID 30086426 (Notch1 activation sustains proliferation, delays differentiation of myeloid progenitors — AML); PMID 39834944 (SMAD1 loss in KMT2A::AFF1/KMT2A::MLLT3 AML); PMID 40274709 (BMP6/SMAD1/5/9 promotes cerebral angiogenesis after ischemic stroke); PMID 34080665 (HOXA11 drives AML progression and cytarabine response); PMID 37059588 (HOXA11-AS regulates ischemic neuronal death via miR-337-3p/YBX1).
how_to_falsify: In a murine KMT2A-rearranged AML model, restore SMAD1 while blocking MAML1/Notch (or vice versa) and check whether HES1/HEY1 and MMP2 co-vary as the shared-node model predicts; separately, in a mouse MCAO stroke model, knock down SMAD1 and ask whether Notch target genes (HES1/HEY1) or HOXA11 protein-level (not HOXA11-AS) expression shift in the peri-infarct vasculature. If SMAD1 and MAML1/Notch activity move independently of each other and of HOXA11 in both systems (no shared HEY1/MMP2 response), the proposed convergent axis is wrong.
caveats: Only 27 patient-group comparisons and 4 independent cohort pairs back these concordance counts, and AML (blood/bone marrow) and stroke (cerebrovascular) are not a natural tissue pairing, so any shared axis is a repurposed-signaling argument, not a shared organ story. HOXA11's stroke support comes from the antisense transcript HOXA11-AS, a distinct regulatory species from the HOXA11 protein driving the AML target set — treat that link as suggestive, not equivalent evidence. PML had the highest AML Open Targets percentile and strong AML literature (APL cases) but was excluded from the carrying set because its 'stroke' hits are confounded with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (same acronym, unrelated disease), not cerebrovascular stroke. ZBTB20 also has independent AML and stroke/hypoxia support plus a review spanning both diseases (PMID 37762065), but its targets (AFP, FBP1, NFKBIA) are metabolic/NF-κB and do not mechanistically overlap with the Notch/BMP/HOX module, so it was left out rather than folded in. None of the tissue-generic exclusions (STAT5A, ERG, GFI1, etc.) were needed to build this account, which argues the axis is narrower than generic hematopoietic/vascular identity, but ZNF76, ZNF304, GTF3A, DMBX1 and several others in the concordant list have no literature at all and were excluded because there was nothing to build on.
